primary.title: Air India CEO gets axe to rejig top deck
primary.description: Mumbai: Air India is overhauling its senior management team, with new chief executive Tewolde Gebremariam seeking to bring in professionals with extensive airline experience as the Tata Group-owned carrier struggles to translate an ambitious expansion programme into a financial turnaround, people familiar with the matter said.Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran has given Gebremariam a free hand to build his team, including hiring external executives with experience in running large airlines, executives said. The changes could see Nipun Aggarwal, currently one of the most influential members of Air India’s leadership, move out of executive management, the people said.136141238Chandrasekaran and Aggarwal have discussed the possibility, with the Tata Sons chairman understood to have offered him alternative roles within the group, they said. Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata is said to have objected to Aggarwal succeeding Campbell Wilson as CEO of Air India. Gebremariam, who led Ethiopian Airlines for more than a decade, took charge of Air India on October 1.Also Read: Adani Airport Holdings to raise Rs 2,790 crore from 360 ONE Asset at $18 billion valuationAir India did not comment.Global Headwinds Hit AirlineThe proposed reset comes as the carrier faces mounting pressure to improve its performance after reporting a consolidated net loss of 22,238.230 crore for the year ended March, more than double that of 10,858.834 crore a year earlier. Consolidated revenue fell to 71,869.943 crore from 78,635.605 crore, according to the airline’s annual report.The pressure on the business was also reflected in its cost base. Consolidated expenses rose to 93,733.314 crore in FY26 from 89,317.124 crore in the previous year as revenue declined. Operating indicators weakened as well. Passenger numbers fell to 36 million in FY26 from 43.8 million a year earlier, while the passenger load factor declined to 81% from 85%.Available seat kilometres, a measure of capacity, fell to 100,828 million from 114,226 million, while revenue passenger kilometres declined to 81,794 million from 96,551 million.The airline has cited geopolitical tensions, airspace closures, longer flight times, payload restrictions and operational disruptions among the challenges affecting performance. The figures underline the task facing Gebremariam: improving reliability and aircraft utilisation while controlling costs and generating stronger returns from the airline’s investments.Aggarwal, Air India’s chief commercial and transformation officer, has been central to the Tata Group’s strategy for the carrier since its takeover in January 2022. He joined the airline after playing a key role in leading its acquisition for Tata Sons and has overseen aircraft procurement and financing, network planning, revenue management, alliances, product development, sales and marketing.Also Read: Air India, Airbus to develop voluntary corporate SAF programmeHe also spearheaded negotiations for Air India’s large aircraft and engine orders, which underpin its fleet expansion plans. Before joining the airline, Aggarwal was a senior vice president at Tata Sons, where he worked on strategy and transformation across group companies. He has more than 30 years of experience spanning corporate finance, mergers and acquisitions and business development, including stints at Bank of America Merrill Lynch, Standard Chartered Bank and BP.Gebremariam is expected to lay greater emphasis on operational discipline, safety, network efficiency and cost control as the airline moves beyond the initial phase of integration and fleet expansion.A key priority is to reassess Air India’s network and hub strategy, including reducing the concentration of operations around Delhi and developing Mumbai and Hyderabad as stronger hubs to improve connectivity, aircraft utilisation and operating efficiency.
